title: Southern Live Oak: Ancient Live Oaks You Can Visit
meta_description: The evergreen oak of the American South, hung with Spanish moss. Charleston's Middleton Oak is put at 900 to 1,000 years and ten metres round.
intro: Southern live oak is the evergreen oak of the humid coastal South, hung with Spanish moss and rarely far from salt air, and its old ones spread wider than they grow tall. The Middleton Oak in Charleston, put at 900 to 1,000 years, was long described as the largest tree in the eastern United States. Brunswick built Albany Street around Lover's Oak rather than through it. In New Orleans the McDonogh Oak rests its heavy branches on wooden crutches, and the Live Oak Society, whose members are the trees themselves, lists the Middleton Oak as its First Vice President. The Emancipation Proclamation got its first public reading in the South under a live oak in Hampton, Virginia, in 1863. In Dealey Plaza the shots at President Kennedy passed through a live oak's canopy, and Pisa has grown one since 1829.
